title: NYSC Mobilisation
summary: Complete guide to the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) mobilisation process. Covers senate list verification, portal registration, pre-camp packing, camp survival, PPA posting, and monthly clearance.

steps.title: Register on the NYSC Portal
steps.body: Check that your institution has uploaded your name to the approved Senate or Academic Board list on the NYSC portal. Once confirmed, create your account, capture your biometrics, fill out your biodata, and pick your state preferences. Check the official portal for current registration timelines.

steps.title: Check Your Call-up Letter & Green Card
steps.body:
When mobilization opens for your stream, download your Green Card and Call-up Letter directly from your dashboard.

Check every detail immediately: your full name spelling, date of birth, course, institution, and deployed state. If anything is wrong, apply for a correction on your dashboard right away before heading to camp. Date of birth corrections require a WAEC verification pin.
tips: Print at least 3 color copies of both your Call-up Letter and Green Card.
Do NOT laminate your Green Card or Call-up Letter — camp officials must stamp and sign them.
Save digital PDF copies on your phone and Google Drive / cloud storage.
steps.warning: Never use third-party agents claiming to change your deployed state for a fee; all official postings are generated directly on the portal.

items.label: Use a government-recognised hospital
items.hint: You may need a medical fitness certificate for camp registration or for requesting a change of posting or relocation, depending on your situation.

items.hint: Keep your original medical certificate safe for physical registration and retain copies for your records.

steps.title: What to Expect at Orientation Camp
steps.body:
Orientation camp lasts for 21 days under military and paramilitary supervision. On Day 1, you go through security screening, registration, biometric clearance, platoon assignment, and kit collection (khaki uniform, crested vest, jungle boots, cap, belt, and PT shorts).

Daily schedule includes the 4:30 AM morning bugle, morning devotion, physical training (PT), military parade drills, SAED skills lectures, and evening social/sports competitions.
tips: Guard your meal ticket, platoon slip, and bunk locker keys carefully.
Join your platoon activities, OBS (radio station), or the camp band to make friends.
Report to the camp clinic right away if you fall sick — doctors and nurses are on 24-hour duty.

steps.title: Your PPA Posting & Relocation Basics
steps.body:
On the final day of camp (Passing Out Parade), you will receive your posting letter to your Place of Primary Assignment (PPA) — usually a public school, government ministry, healthcare facility, or vetted private organization.

Take your posting letter to your assigned employer within 48 hours for acceptance or rejection. If rejected, take the signed rejection letter back to your Local Government Inspector (LGI) for reposting. Relocation on marital or medical grounds is applied for inside camp before the close of orientation.
tips: Never stay in an unapproved PPA without official documentation; unauthorized absence can lead to extension of service.
Ask your employer early about accommodation or transport support.
Keep a stamped copy of your employer's acceptance letter for your LGI documentation.

items.label: Get your posting letter
items.hint: After camp you are posted to a Place of Primary Assignment, and you can ask to be relocated through the NYSC state office.

items.label: Speak to your Local Government Inspector or state coordinator
items.hint: Discuss posting placement or relocation procedures with your assigned officials.

items.label: Prepare any supporting documents they ask for
items.hint: Rules differ by state and change often. Confirm with your NYSC state secretariat.

steps.title: CDS Groups & Monthly Clearance
steps.body:
Throughout your service year, you will belong to a Community Development Service (CDS) group that meets once a week for community projects.

To receive your monthly Federal Government stipend (allawee), you must complete your monthly biometric clearance at your Local Government Secretariat. Your PPA employer must sign your monthly evaluation letter, which you present to your LGI.
tips: Sign your weekly CDS attendance register faithfully.
Do your biometric clearance early during the clearance window each month.
If you need to travel outside your state, submit an official leave request through your LGI to the State Coordinator.
